text: Kingsmoor FC initiated the match by winning a high-pressure situation inside the box, earning a penalty converted by Viktor Quinlan at 8' after aggressive pressing forced defensive errors [#152]. The subsequent goal at 12' featured an 8-pass sequence from a regain, exemplifying their wide 4-4-2 formation with quick combination play and moderate first half PPDA of 13.3, maintaining possession to build overloads in advanced areas [#222]. Westport Albion countered with rapid transition goals at 22' and 30' relying on vertical direct passes, demonstrating effective fast breaks from regains with fewer passes, tailoring to their direct 4-4-2 style and lower PPDA of 7.8 in the first half [#401] [#553]. Kingsmoor’s tactical shift at 65' increased press intensity (from 0.5 to 0.68) and line height (to 0.62), aiming for higher turnovers and quicker forward progression, though it increased their turnovers and failed to immediately raise xG [#1187]. Westport reacted by dropping their press and tempo at 79' to absorb pressure and rest defence, modifying their style to reduce Kingsmoor’s field tilt [#1459]. Despite a late red card on Felix Barros, Kingsmoor maintained wide play and crossing to score a late goal at 82', underscoring their persistent use of quick transitions and field width even under numerical disadvantage [#1516] [#1495].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for analyst audience in en

- Kingsmoor FC scored 3 goals with a total xG of 3.3 from 10 shots and 3 big chances [#152, #222, #1516].
- Viktor Quinlan (Kingsmoor FC) scored 2 goals with a combined xG of 1.26 and earned player of the match with rating 9.8 [#152, #222].
- Westport Albion scored 3 goals with a total xG of 3.41 from 18 shots and 3 big chances [#401, #553, #983].
- Felix Barros of Kingsmoor FC received a second yellow and was sent off at 81' [#1494, #1495].
- Tactical change by Kingsmoor FC at 65' to press higher and play direct did not immediately increase xG [#1187].

- Kingsmoor FC took an early lead through a penalty by Viktor Quinlan at 8', showing they were able to win a high-pressure situation inside the box, possibly due to aggressive pressing or forcing a defensive error from Westport Albion [#152].  
- The second goal by Quinlan at 12' came after an 8-pass, 27-second build-up starting from a regain, indicating Kingsmoor's effective use of quick combination play and maintaining possession after recovery, consistent with their 4-4-2 wide crossing style and a moderate PPDA of 13.3 in the first half [#222].  
- Westport Albion responded with two rapid goals by Rafael Delacroix at 22' and 30', both following regains and involving vertical and direct passing sequences with relatively few passes, reflecting their 4-4-2 direct style focusing on quick transitions and penetrating runs in behind the defense [#401, #553].  
- The equalizer for Westport at 51' by Kenji Rahman came from a short build-up (4 passes in 29 seconds) and a cross assist, showing their ability to capitalize on wide areas and deliver effective crosses into the box, aligning with their vertical passing style but also exploiting Kingsmoor’s defensive width [#983].  
- In the second half, Kingsmoor FC shifted to a more intense pressing and directness approach around the 65th minute, increasing their press intensity from 0.5 to 0.68 and line height to 0.62 to chase the game. This tactical change aimed at recovering possession higher and faster, possibly to create overloads and quick attacking opportunities, though it came with increased turnovers [#1187].  
- Westport Albion responded tactically at 79' by dropping deeper, slowing tempo, and reducing pressing intensity to protect their lead. This likely aimed to absorb pressure and force Kingsmoor to play in less dangerous areas, consistent with their style shift from high PPDA and intensity to a more conservative defensive posture [#1459].  
- The late 82' goal for Kingsmoor through Luca Iversen came from a quick regain and two-pass move culminating in a cross from Mason Morales, highlighting Kingsmoor's continued emphasis on wide play and crossing under increased pressing pressure, despite being a man down after Barros’ red card at 81' [#1516, #1495].
